label: H.R. 9495

latest_action.text: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 621.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9495 provides fiscal year 2027 appropriations for the Department of Defense and related military activities, excluding military construction, family housing, Army Corps of Engineers civil works, and nuclear warheads. It sets funding levels for military personnel, operation and maintenance, procurement, research and development, revolving funds, and specific defense programs. Additionally, the bill includes administrative requirements, restrictions, and policy provisions governing defense funds, contracting, and intelligence activities.

affected_groups.effect: Receive pay, allowances, training, healthcare support, and retirement fund contributions funded by the bill.
affected_groups.group: Military personnel and reserves of the United States Armed Forces

affected_groups.effect: Subject to federal acquisition rules, domestic sourcing requirements, business process changes, and restrictions on arbitration agreements and funding uses.
affected_groups.group: Department of Defense civilian employees and defense contractors

key_provisions: Provides appropriations for military personnel across the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force, as well as reserve and National Guard components.
Funds operation and maintenance accounts for military branches, defense-wide activities, and specialized funds such as the Counter-ISIS Train and Equip Fund.
Allocates funding for procurement, including aircraft, missiles, weapons, tracked combat vehicles, ammunition, shipbuilding and conversion, and the Defense Production Act.
Funds basic and applied research, development, test, and evaluation programs across the military departments and defense-wide agencies.

Provides appropriations for other defense programs and related agencies, including the Combat and Operational Medicine Program, TRICARE Private Sector Care, chemical munitions destruction, drug interdiction, and the Office of Inspector General.
Sets various general provisions and restrictions regarding the use of funds, multiyear procurement contracts, domestic sourcing requirements, and intelligence activities.
